extraction_scope: Source-reviewed final mechanism ontology bounded to local XML/PDF/figure/supplement evidence; no unsupported intracellular target is claimed.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: C18G and cationic side-chain variants bind anionic PC/PG lipid vesicles more strongly than neutral PC vesicles, supporting membrane-selective interaction as context for antimicrobial activity.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: C18G, C18G-Arg, C18G-His, C18G-Orn, and C18G-Dap
mechanism_claims.limitations: Vesicle binding is model-membrane evidence and is not by itself a direct bacterial killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The peptides directly permeabilize E. coli membranes to different extents in nitrocefin outer-membrane and ONPG inner-membrane assays; C18G, C18G-Arg, and C18G-Orn are the strongest outer-membrane permeabilizers, while C18G-His and C18G-Dap are weak in these assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: C18G variant panel in E. coli D31 assays
direct_assay_types: beta-lactamase nitrocefin outer membrane permeability assay
beta-galactosidase ONPG inner membrane permeability assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure/time-course values were not digitized; claim is qualitative and comparative.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The peptides permeabilize S. aureus membranes in a propidium iodide flow-cytometry assay, with C18G-Arg and C18G-Orn showing strong permeabilization over lower concentrations than several other variants.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: C18G variant panel in S. aureus ATCC 27660 assay
direct_assay_types: propidium iodide uptake by flow cytometry
mechanism_claims.limitations: Claim is limited to membrane permeability; no intracellular molecular target is asserted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The peptide panel shows low sheep red-blood-cell hemolysis at tested concentrations, with C18G giving the highest reported approximate hemolysis at the 15 uM concentration.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: C18G variant panel in sheep RBC assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is toxicity/selectivity context, not a bacterial mechanism claim.
